101.intention: Learn that an anchor interrupts a glide: Blue stops at two adjacent interior anchors before turning home. This single-resident reminder isolates the new rule.

102.intention: Mint uses the right-column anchor as an interior launch point for its nest approach. Remove the decorative corner anchor so the highlighted stop is the actual lesson.

103.intention: Gold reaches the left-column anchor and launches horizontally toward home. Contrast the previous vertical approach; remove the corner tile that never changes movement.

104.intention: Lavender establishes the row-one anchor stop while Blue has a separate short approach. Introduce reading two residents without requiring a new cooperation chain yet.

105.intention: Coral changes direction from the interior row-two anchor before Mint completes its approach. Read the new fixed stop separately from residents that can move away.

106.intention: Gold parks on the bottom-row anchor to stop Blue one cell to its right; Blue turns home before Gold finishes. Open the redundant rock so the anchor, not the neighboring rock, creates Gold's position.

107.intention: Blue uses the upper-row anchor to obtain a precise launch column while Coral finishes a short contrasting approach. Practice recognizing an anchor even on the board edge.

108.intention: Coral approaches the lower interior anchor before changing direction home. Its longer setup contrasts Blue's shorter route without adding an untaught tile.

109.intention: Blue uses the row-two interior anchor after Lavender's setup. Distinguish stopping on a tile from stopping immediately before a resident.

110.intention: Coral launches from the right-side anchor and uses Mint at the left edge as a temporary stop. Mint's position is a natural edge stop, not an anchor placement; keep that distinction explicit.

111.intention: Blue uses Gold in two different columns, with Gold's interior anchor stop between those services. Do not capture the relocated helper before Blue's second downward approach.

112.intention: Mint first uses Lavender near the bottom-right corner; Lavender then visits two right-column anchors on its own approach. Contrast an ordinary helper stop with exact tile stops.

113.intention: Coral launches from the bottom-row anchor using Gold at the right edge; after Coral arrives home, Gold reuses the same anchor. One fixed tile supports two sequential routes.

114.intention: Blue reaches the left-side anchor before stopping against Lavender along the top row. Plan the launch direction rather than treating every anchor as a destination.

115.intention: Coral uses the central anchor for a real stop. Compare Mint's different incoming direction at that location: an anchor label alone does not prove that it changed a glide.

116.intention: Blue parks on the left-side anchor, creating Coral's horizontal turn point. Coral goes home first; Blue must remain available until that shared approach is complete.

117.intention: Blue launches from the upper anchor and uses Coral below it; after Blue goes home, Coral reuses that anchor. Share a launch tile while preserving the helper until its service is finished.

118.intention: Coral occupies the right-column anchor so Blue can stop immediately beneath it. Blue captures first, releasing Coral for its own nest approach.

119.intention: Blue makes an initial anchor stop, then Coral parks on the interior row-two anchor for Blue's horizontal approach. Separate the first launch setup from the later helper placement.

120.intention: Coral launches left from the right-edge anchor and uses Blue as its stop. Blue finishes first only after that launch has established Coral's route.

121.intention: Mint supplies Coral's first stop, then relocates onto the left-side anchor to serve Blue. Finish Coral and Blue before releasing Mint; all three residents contribute to the chain.

122.intention: Mint launches from its interior anchor using Blue, while Blue later relies on Coral below. Keep Mint available through the two-resident relay, then capture it last.

123.intention: Gold launches from the upper interior anchor against Coral on the left, then Coral uses Gold in the right column. Reciprocal helper roles connect the anchor setup to the capture order.

124.intention: Coral launches horizontally from the lower anchor toward Blue's temporary stop. This shorter two-resident contrast asks for direction and release timing rather than extra board clutter.

125.intention: Mint's first anchor setup enables Blue's initial approach; Blue then parks on a second anchor to stop Coral. Capture Blue, Coral, then Mint only after the relay has done its work.

126.intention: Mint first stops Blue on the left side, then stops Coral after Coral launches from the right anchor. One helper serves two travelers before it can finish last.

127.intention: Coral parks on an interior anchor to stop Mint, and Mint's new position stops Blue. Capture Blue and Mint before releasing the original anchor helper.

128.intention: Blue and Coral reuse the bottom anchor, then each stops the other in a different row. This two-resident reciprocal puzzle depends on relocation, not simply two independent anchor errands.

129.intention: Coral launches from the upper anchor using Blue below, and Mint later uses Blue on the right. Blue must serve both routes before Mint can complete the chain.

130.intention: Blue first uses Coral on the right edge, then parks on the interior anchor to stop Mint. A resident changes from traveler to helper before its final capture.

136.intention: Mint launches from the interior anchor against relocated Coral on the right. Mint's new position then stops Blue below: a two-stage launch-to-helper relay precedes all captures.

138.intention: Blue initially stops Mint near the bottom; Coral later parks on the upper anchor to provide Mint's second stop. Mint captures first only after both distinct helpers have served it.

139.intention: Mint uses Coral on the right edge and relocates upward to stop Blue launching from its anchor. Blue's second anchor approach follows the shared setup; all residents remain connected.

148.intention: Coral and Blue supply Mint's two initial stops; Mint relocates to stop Blue launching from the top anchor, and Blue's new position stops Coral horizontally. Capture Coral, Mint, then Blue only after this four-service reciprocal chain is complete.

149.intention: Mint stops Blue across the top, Blue stops Coral, and Coral then stops Mint on that same row. Blue needs Mint again before Coral parks on the interior anchor for Blue's final approach: five services across a shared passage precede the first capture.

150.intention: Blue stops Coral on the top row and Mint supplies its second turn near the bottom. Delay Coral's final anchor placement while Blue completes its route; Coral then stops Mint before capturing, leaving Mint to finish last. The final service occurs after the first capture, unlike the preceding all-services-first relay.
